## Continuation

```{r}
year = 2025

crash_url = paste0('https://www.planecrashinfo.com/', year, '/', year, '.htm')

crash_page <- rvest::read_html(crash_url, encoding = "ISO-8859-1")

# This should now print without the error
crash_page

# How many <table> elements are on the page?
crash_tables <- crash_page |>
  rvest::html_elements("table") |>
  rvest::html_table()

# From a cleaning perspective: 
# [1] Obviously, translate this into a DF instead of a list 
# [2] To replace the current headers with row 1 and then delete row 1 
# [3] Convert Date into a data column instead of chr
# [4] More complex cleaning to split multiple information within a cell into separate columns(outside of the scope of today's class -- feel free to try AI or regular expressiosn if you are in 414)

# back to our pepper shaker analogy 
crash_df = crash_tables[[1]] # Subsetting a list 

colnames(crash_df) = crash_df[1, ]
crash_df = crash_df[-1, ]


# convert Date column into date type obj 
crash_df = crash_df |> 
  dplyr:: mutate(Date = lubridate::dmy(Date))

dplyr::glimpse(crash_df)

```



## In class game activity 
```{r game}
page = rvest::read_html("https://isa401-salvage.vercel.app/registry?start=1")
classes = page |>
  rvest::html_elements(".Dreadnought") |>
  rvest::html_text2()
length(classes)   # check this first: one per card



## Stage 3 
base = "https://isa401-salvage.vercel.app"
starts = seq(from = 1, to = 351, by = 50)
pages = vector("list", length(starts)) # intializing the list [Similar to initialing the data frame (df)]
for (i in seq_along(starts)) {
  pg = rvest::read_html(paste0(base, "/registry?start=", starts[i]))
  pages[[i]] = data.frame(
    class = pg |> rvest::html_elements("div > ul > li:nth-child(1) > span") |> 
      rvest::html_text2(),
    value = pg |> rvest::html_elements("div > ul > li:nth-child(3) > span") |> 
       rvest::html_text2() |> readr::parse_number()
  )
  Sys.sleep(1)   # robots.txt asks for it
}
registry = dplyr::bind_rows(pages)   # 400 rows?

registry |> 
  dplyr::filter(class == "Dreadnought")

sum(Dreadnought_df$value)

Dreadnought_df <- registry |>
  dplyr::filter(class == "Dreadnought")

```


## ISA 125 Extraction

```{r}
chat = ellmer::chat_openai(
  model = "gpt-5.6-luna"
)

isa125_courseblock = rvest::read_html("https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/") |> 
  rvest::html_element("#sc_sccoursedescs > div:nth-child(1)") |> 
  rvest::html_text2()


chat$chat_structured(
isa125_courseblock,
type = ellmer::type_object(
# code is the name of the first element in the returned sub-list 
# type_string -> forces that element or be of type chr
  code = ellmer::type_string( 
    description = " The three letter abbreviation for the course and its number. For example, ISA 999 or FIN 444"), 
  name = ellmer::type_string( "The title of the course without the three letter abbreviation and the number. For example, Intoduction to Macroeconomics. Does not return a period after the name"), 
  cr_hr = ellmer::type_integer(description = "The number of credits shown in parantheses after the course code and title")
))

```


## All 50 ISA Courses

```{r all_isa_courses}
course_vec= rvest::read_html("https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/") |> 
  rvest::html_elements(".courseblock") |> rvest::html_text2()

# Similar to https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/articles/structured-data.html
course_list = as.list(course_vec)

type_course =  ellmer::type_object(
# code is the name of the first element in the returned sub-list 
# type_string -> forces that element or be of type chr
  code = ellmer::type_string( 
    description = " The three letter abbreviation for the course and its number. For example, ISA 999 or FIN 444"), 
  name = ellmer::type_string( "The title of the course without the three letter abbreviation and the number. For example, Intoduction to Macroeconomics. Does not return a period after the name"), 
  cr_hr = ellmer::type_integer(description = "The number of credits shown in parantheses after the course code and title")
)

isa_df = ellmer::parallel_chat_structured(
  chat, prompts = course_list, type = type_course, 
  include_tokens = T, include_cost = T 
)

sum(isa_df$cost)
```
